source_files: lessons/lesson-77/Traducciones con Olvidársele, Caérsele, Rompérsele, Perdérsele, y Acabársele.pdf
target_pattern: Frame unplanned loss, drops, breaks, forgetfulness, and running out with se + IO pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les) + verb; the affected thing is the grammatical subject and controls verb number.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Using I forgot / I dropped / I broke with the person as subject, as if the event were fully intentional.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Spanish often externalizes the event: the thing happens to you. Se marks unplanned occurrence, the IO pronoun marks who is affected, and the lost/broken/forgotten item is the subject.
target_pattern_formula: forget: Se me olvido / Se me olvidaron + thing + (place)
drop: Se me cayo / Se me cayeron + thing
break: Se me rompio / Se nos rompieron + thing
lose/misplace: Se le perdio / Se me perdieron + thing + (place)
run out: Se me acabo / Se nos acabaron + thing
optional clarifier: A Maria se le perdio el pasaporte.
natural_examples: Se me olvido el celular en casa.
Se le cayo la tarjeta de credito.
A Maria se le perdio el pasaporte en el aeropuerto.

controlled_recombination.instructions: Write each sentence in Spanish using the accidental se + IO pronoun pattern.
prompts_en: I forgot my cellphone at home.
She forgot her keys at work.
You dropped your credit card.
They dropped their cameras.
Our window broke.
Javier's headphones broke.
Maria lost her passport at the airport.
I lost my gloves.
The team ran out of space in their suitcases.
We ran out of excuses.
I forgot the meeting link at the office.
He dropped his phone on the stairs.
Their laptop broke during the trip.
We lost the receipt for the expense report.
She ran out of battery on her phone.
You forgot your badge at home.
They broke the projector remote.
I dropped the contract pages in the hallway.
The client lost the signed copy at the hotel.
We ran out of time in the presentation.

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as directed.
drills: Base: Se me olvido el celular en casa. -> change to plural keys at work.
Base: Se le cayo la tarjeta de credito. -> change to they dropped cameras.
Base: Se nos rompio la ventana. -> name Javier and use headphones.
Base: A Maria se le perdio el pasaporte en el aeropuerto. -> change to I lost gloves.
Base: Se nos acabaron las excusas. -> change to team ran out of suitcase space.
Base: Se me olvido el enlace de la reunion. -> change to negative: I did not forget...
Base: Se le cayo el telefono en las escaleras. -> change subject to you (tu).
Base: Se les rompio la laptop durante el viaje. -> change to present: the screen is breaking.
Base: Se nos perdio el recibo. -> add place: at the restaurant.
Base: Se le acabo la bateria del telefono. -> change to we ran out of time.
Base: Se te olvido la credencial en casa. -> change to question: Did you forget...?
Base: Se les cayeron las paginas del contrato. -> change to singular page.
Base: Se le perdio la copia firmada en el hotel. -> clarify client with A el cliente.
Base: Se me cayeron los guantes. -> change verb to break.
Base: Se nos acabo el tiempo. -> change to run out of coffee.

contrastive_discrimination.instructions: Choose the natural Spanish sentence for unplanned/affected-party framing.
prompts: I forgot my phone at home. (Olvide mi celular en casa. vs Se me olvido el celular en casa.)
I dropped the card. (Cai la tarjeta. vs Se me cayo la tarjeta.)
The window broke on us. (Rompimos la ventana. vs Se nos rompio la ventana.)
She lost her passport. (Perdio su pasaporte. vs Se le perdio el pasaporte.)
We ran out of time. (Acabamos el tiempo. vs Se nos acabo el tiempo.)
I forgot the keys (plural). (Se me olvido las llaves. vs Se me olvidaron las llaves.)
They dropped the cameras. (Se les cayo las camaras. vs Se les cayeron las camaras.)
I fell down the stairs. (Se me cai en las escaleras. vs Me cai en las escaleras.)
I broke the phone on purpose. (Se me rompio el telefono. vs Rompi el telefono.)
Maria lost her passport. (A Maria le perdio el pasaporte. vs A Maria se le perdio el pasaporte.)

reverse_conceptual_expression.instructions: Write natural Spanish with accidental se framing; do not use literal I-forgot/I-dropped subject patterns.
prompts_en: My wallet stayed at home — I didn't mean to leave it.
Her ID fell out of her bag on the bus.
Our microwave stopped working unexpectedly.
He can't find the USB drive he had this morning.
We have no more coffee in the office.
I left the documents at the client site by mistake.
Your pen fell on the floor just now.
Their rental car got a flat tire.
She's out of phone storage again.
The team used up all the budget for this quarter.

common_errors.why_it_happens: English puts the person as intentional subject instead of accidental se frame.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Se me olvido el celular en casa.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Plural subject does not trigger plural verb agreement.
Caerse reflexive for person falling is mixed with thing dropping.
Active we-broke framing is used for an unplanned break.
Simple transitive lose replaces affected-party se pattern.
Possessive is added even though affected item is already the subject.

common_errors.mistake: A Maria le perdio el pasaporte
common_errors.why_it_happens: Accidental se is omitted before IO pronoun.
common_errors.correct_spanish: A Maria se le perdio el pasaporte.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Run-out event is expressed as direct transitive action.
IO pattern for thing dropping is confused with person falling (me cai).
